implemented_requirements.evidence: Board class defines ROWS = 6 and COLS = 7 and creates a 6×7 grid in board.py.
Game stores two Player objects, tracks current_index, and switches turn with switch_turn() after each move (game.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players choose columns by typing a number
implemented_requirements.evidence: prompt_column() reads input() and converts it to an int (game.py).
drop_disc() places the disc in the lowest empty cell and Game.play prints board.render() after each turn (board.py, game.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Horizontal, vertical and diagonal win detection
implemented_requirements.evidence: check_win() scans four DIRECTIONS ((0,1),(1,0),(1,1),(1,-1)) and counts consecutive discs (board.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when the grid is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full() checks every cell; Game.play ends with a draw message if true (board.py, game.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Validate column choices (range, integer, not full)
implemented_requirements.evidence: prompt_column() validates integer conversion, uses Board.is_valid_column() and Board.column_is_full() (game.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: End the game on win or draw
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.play returns after printing a win or draw message (game.py).

judge.summary: All core Connect Four features are fully implemented: a 6×7 board, two alternating players, numeric column input with validation, real‑time board rendering, win detection in all directions, draw detection, and graceful termination. The code is self‑contained and appears ready to run.
